name: workshop-inventory-is-real
description:
The first e2e coverage of the agent builder: a real agent session calling `workshop_inventory` gets answers from the REAL pkg/tools/workshopmcp.Server (test/e2e/workshop_mcp.go's mountWorkshopMCP), running against the harness's real envtest apiserver — not the canned MCPStub every other sidecar bundle in this corpus dispatches through. driver.go's sidecar-probe routing closure matches on this bundle's SidecarToolbox CR name ("workshop", the workshopSidecarToolboxRef constant) and sends its calls to h.WorkshopMCPURL() instead of h.MCP.URL().

Three facts are asserted, each provable ONLY by a real handleInventory reading real cluster state — a canned MCP stub has no SpiceboxClassList, no ClusterAgentSettings, and no apimage registry to answer from:
  1. sandboxClasses reports the fixture's own SpiceboxClass ("workshop-sandbox"), read via a live SpiceboxClassList.
  2. ceilings.budget.maxTurns reports the fixture's own ClusterAgentSettings ceiling (91), read via a live Get of the cluster-scoped singleton — which handleInventory refuses to answer at all without (see tools_inventory.go: it errors if it cannot Get one).
  3. sidecarImages reports ap-api-adapter with a `ref` — plan 8a's WorkshopSidecarImages discovery path (pkg/platform/apimage), proving itself end to end through a real session for the first time.

Each is checked with its own `workshop_inventory` call (the tool is read-only and idempotent, so three real dispatches against three cluster reads is the natural way this format asserts three distinct facts from one JSON result — Expect.LastToolResultContains is a single substring per step).

Verified FAIL-FIRST per plan (see task-3-report.md): with the driver's routing closure temporarily repointed at h.MCP.URL() for the workshop ref too, this bundle fails at the FIRST workshop_inventory call — the stub has no tools/list entry for it at all (no ToolOutputs was ever registered, because this bundle deliberately carries none), so the sidecar's own tool synthesis fails closed before the model even gets a turn. That is the right failure: a bundle that would also pass against the stub proves nothing about the real server.

WHAT THIS BUNDLE DOES NOT PROVE: it does not exercise the production Workshop-Ready->sidecar-identity path, which does not exist yet. RunModeFor (pkg/controllers/agentsession/sidecars.go) returns RunModeSeparatePod — the only run mode that ever gets a minted WorkshopIdentity via BuildSidecarPod's identity branch — only when a SidecarToolbox declares spec.secretInputs, and the shipped workshop toolbox (pkg/tools/workshopmcp/deploy/sidecartoolbox.yaml, copied verbatim into this bundle's fixture) declares none. So this fixture's workshop toolbox runs IN-POD, same as every other sidecar bundle in this corpus, and mountWorkshopMCP hands the real Server a synthetic WorkshopIdentity directly rather than one minted by that (nonexistent) production path. A green run here is evidence the workshop TOOLS work against real cluster state; it is not evidence the identity plumbing that would hand them a live one is wired — see mountWorkshopMCP's own doc comment for the same statement at the code that would first need to change.
userTurns: Look at this cluster's real capabilities and tell me what sandbox class, turn ceiling, and sidecar image you'd build with.

expect.userTextContains: sandbox class, turn ceiling, and sidecar image

args._reason: need the cluster's real sandbox classes before proposing a build
confirm the cluster's governance ceiling before proposing a budget
confirm the admitted sidecar images before proposing an adapter

reply.text: This cluster's real inventory: the workshop-sandbox SpiceboxClass, a 91-turn governance ceiling, and the ap-api-adapter sidecar image for REST-API tool adapters.

args.summary: reported the cluster's real inventory: sandbox class, ceiling, and sidecar image
